draft_evidence.quote:
Thornwater on the ninety-third day, from the road below the ford, in the afternoon.

He counted it because it had been thirty-five days. The wall, and the gate in it, and on the gate-walk the bowman, who was the same bowman, and who had seen five people on the road and had called nothing down, which was a verdict of its own. The ford below the wall with its stones, and no dogs on them. The grain loft's roof, where the season's first log had been written. Smoke from two chimneys. And at the gate itself, tied to the post, a second mule, with panniers, and a bench pulled into the wall's shade, and a woman on the bench with a carter's hand in both of hers.

She did not look up. She was counting, and he knew the count, and it went to ten.

"That's a hand," she said to the carter. "You'll keep it dry and you'll not lift with it for six days, and if you lift with it in five you'll not lie to me about it, because I'll know." The carter took the hand back and went in at the gate. Then she looked up.

She looked at Lira's feet first, the two boots, and at the leg above the carter's boot, and nodded once at the leg. Brom's forearm, carrying a box by strap and not pulling anything: nothing. Karis's hands, the pen in the healed one: a look, no longer than a count of one. Seln: nothing, because there was nothing on him. Then Cael, and the side he carried the satchel away from, and she looked at the tape through the shirt as if the shirt were not there.

"Seventeen days," she said.

"Seventeen."

"Breath stops at it."

"At the tape."

"It'll do that till it's off." She stood, without hurry and without spending anything on it, and untied the mule's lead from the post one-handed. "Ninth day. I said nine. You've counted."

"Ninety-third."

comparison_evidence.quote:
She taped his ribs on the eighty-first morning, before the sun was on the bench, and told him what it was while she did it.

"This is cloth," Oryn said. "Anybody can do cloth. Breathe out. All of it." She took the linen round him under the arm and over the place three times, pulling at each turn until the breath he had left stopped where she wanted it and not where the shale-back had decided. "There. Now it stops at the tape. That's the whole of what tape does. It doesn't mend anything. It tells the ribs where the edge is so they stop looking for it." She tied it off at the front, flat, with the knot where a strap would not lie. "You'll hate it by noon. Leave it."

findings.consequence: The series foregrounds exact day arithmetic and Oryn's clinical precision. Day ninety-three is twelve days after the tape was applied on day eighty-one; the ribs were broken on day seventy-eight, fifteen elapsed days earlier. Calling either state seventeen days makes a careful reader distrust the injury ledger and the otherwise exact ninth-day payoff.
findings.repair_target: Reconcile Oryn's stated count with the established day eighty-one taping and day seventy-eight break while preserving day ninety-three at Thornwater and her clinical register.

draft_evidence.quote: Oryn walked like a carter. He had catalogued it on the mountain and he catalogued it again on the flat because the flat showed it better: economical, sure-footed, never fast. She did not look at the ground and never once put a foot wrong on it. She did not look back. When the mule stopped she stopped, and when it went she went. Lira, twenty paces ahead, looked back at her twice in the first hour and then did not look again, which was Lira deciding a thing was what it was.

comparison_evidence.quote: She walked like a carter: the pace set once at the start of a road and not changed for a slope or a narrow or anything short of an animal in the road; the feet going down whole and staying down; the weight never once ahead of them. Lira moved as if the ground were a thing she could leave. Oryn moved as if it were a thing she had an arrangement with. She was never fast. In four days he did not see her hurry, and he was watching for it — at the mule's stumbles, at the place on the second day where the ground went out from under Brom's box — and she came to each at the same walk, and was there when she was needed and not before. Item. She walked on the down-slope side of the mule, where a rider would come off. Item. She looked at the four of them who could walk as Seln looked at a road, every halt, once, all together, and then at whichever one had changed. Item. She had a heel gone raw in her boot from the mountain, and at the first halt she took the boot off and washed it and taped it with the same grey cloth she had put round his ribs, and put the boot back on, and walked. She did not put her hands on it and go still. She could not do that to herself. She had said so on the bench, and here it was, in a boot.

The otherwise deliberate next-appearance injury inventory therefore lets this minor wound vanish without recurrence or explicit resolution, contrary to the injury-persistence gate.
findings.repair_target: At Oryn's next-appearance inventory, either carry the heel's current effect or explicitly establish that it healed during the nine-day interval; preserve her economical walking and route competence.

Taste only: the boundary sequence deliberately repeats 'same place,' 'same stride,' 'same line,' and 'same step.' This repetition is functional measurement rather than an anti-tic defect, but the audiobook pass should preserve escalation so the procedural refrain does not flatten into redundancy.
strengths: Yes: the worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. The registry's worldview is a printed standard—verified endpoints, brands, solid roads, dashes, and blank paper—tested under Cael's feet against ruts, carts, fords, a failed traverse, and a carter's competing map. The title becomes both object and argument without a detached lore lecture.

There is no fight, exactly as the prohibited outcomes require. The last-mile discovery is nevertheless a memorable set piece whose terrain is load-bearing: thinning scrub exposes the whole approach; the low ridge and shoulder force the road's bend; the shared stride creates the line; ten paces back establishes procedure; the stone fixes memory; the falling light reveals the ring and then leaves Oryn's hands empty. Because there is no combat victory, an 'X removed Y's ability to Z' win sentence is correctly not applicable.

The two maps are unusually efficient thematic objects. Cael's registry sheet turns institutional refusal into negative space, while Karis's carter copy encodes local survival by bending around unnamed circles. Her exact line—'Their map has no roads. His has no quiet ground. Between them you get the country.'—deserves protection in any repair.

Oryn's participation preserves her independent want. She treats the crew as one added stop, names the day she will owe elsewhere, works nine patients before leaving, and walks beside her mule rather than being absorbed into the party by narration. 'Six on the Fallow road' lands once and is not underlined.

The letters carry emotional and institutional movement through physical objects and distinct voices. Ephram reports weather in ordered restraint; Bracken weaponizes truthful blank space; Vell answers resignation by entering an unprecedented ledger line. Cael's reactions remain filing, shelf placement, paper, and reading order rather than announced feeling.

The boundary turn is staged in the body before the mind and gives each person a specific response: Lira gets density, Brom closure, Oryn raised healer's hands, Karis instrument failure, and Seln procedure. Identical failure is observed at a stride without a theory, making the Book 9 plant clean and audible.

Cael's silence is earned rather than coy. The chapter establishes his four-year-dark Arbiter before the line, records no change in either direction, shows why nobody looks to him, and gives him two narrow reasons for withholding. The exact log then fixes the fact while refusing interpretation.

The final image obeys both the packet and the scene-closer rule. Chapter 8's terminal log becomes a mid-chapter record here; prose continues into camp, ridge, broken uprights, water-like light, and Oryn lowering her hands after the floor and ridge go dark.
